description: Composite figure (eight image panels plus a mechanism schematic) comparing μ-DIC experiments with finite-element (FE) simulation of TiB₂-particle behaviour in a low-density steel. Top block, "Global engineering strain = 5 %": (a) SEM image with a 20 μm scale bar, red boxes marking Particle 1 and Particle 2, and cropped SEM insets labelled "Particle 1 fracture" and "Particle 2 fracture"; (a₁) Von-Mises equivalent strain map (colourbar 0.00–0.50); (a₂) PEEQ map (colourbar 0.000–0.500) with a yellow-boxed region and the same fracture insets; (a₃) σ₁₁ (MPa, 0–1000) versus Engineering strain (%, 0–14) for Particle 1 and Particle 2, with arrows marking "Fracture". Lower block, "Global engineering strain = 7 %": (b) SEM with 20 μm scale bar and red boxes for Particle 3 and Particle 4; (b₁) μ-DIC equivalent-strain map; (b₂) PEEQ map with insets "Particle 3 decohesion" and "Particle 4 fracture"; (b₃) σ₁₁ (0–1800 MPa) versus Engineering strain (%, 0–14) with arrows "Decohesion" and "Fracture". (c) is a three-stage schematic of void initiation with a legend for TiB₂ Particle, δ-Ferrite, Austenite, Plastic slip band, Dislocation, TiB₂ Particle cracking void and Interfacial debonding void. The figure demonstrates that μ-DIC and FE strain fields correspond, with strain gradients localised at particles, and that particle fracture precedes particle decohesion.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph at 5 % global engineering strain with a 20 μm scale bar; red boxes mark two particles (Particle 1, upper centre; Particle 2, lower left), and two cropped SEM insets to the right are labelled 'Particle 1 fracture' (top) and 'Particle 2 fracture' (bottom), showing cracked particles.

Blue-scale map labelled at the colourbar as 'Von-Mises equivalent strain' spanning 0.00–0.50 with ticks every 0.10; shows a largely uniform low-strain field with faint darker patches outlining particle shapes.

PEEQ (plastic equivalent strain) contour map, colourbar 0.000–0.500 with ticks 0.000/0.125/0.250/0.375/0.500, a yellow rectangular outline in the lower-left, and insets 'Particle 1 fracture' and 'Particle 2 fracture' showing localised high-strain (cyan/yellow) regions adjacent to the particles.

σ₁₁ stress history (MPa, y-axis 0–1000) versus Engineering strain (%, x-axis 0–14); legend entries 'Particle 1' (grey open symbols) and 'Particle 2' (red open symbols); black arrows labelled 'Fracture' mark the abrupt stress drops, with small inset maps of the corresponding particles.

SEM micrograph at 7 % global engineering strain, 20 μm scale bar; red boxes mark Particle 3 (upper left) and Particle 4 (right), with cropped insets labelled 'Particle 3 decohesion' and 'Particle 4 fracture'.
Von-Mises equivalent strain map (colourbar 0.00–0.50) at 7 % strain with a green arrow pointing to a locally strained region.
PEEQ map (colourbar 0.000–0.500) with a yellow-boxed region, a red arrow indicating a localised band, and insets 'Particle 3 decohesion' and 'Particle 4 fracture'.

σ₁₁ stress history (MPa, y-axis up to 1800) versus Engineering strain (%, 0–14) for 'Particle 3' (grey) and 'Particle 4' (red); arrows label the events 'Decohesion' and 'Fracture', with inset particle maps.

Schematic diagram, three stacked stages, of microstructure evolution and deformation mechanism of low-density steel: yellow TiB₂ particles in a matrix of pink austenite and light-blue δ-ferrite, magenta plastic slip bands, dislocation symbols, black cracking voids inside particles and interfacial debonding voids at particle/matrix interfaces; legend lists all symbols used.

observations.observation: The group is composite, containing SEM images, μ-DIC equivalent-strain maps, FE PEEQ maps, σ₁₁-versus-strain curves and a mechanism schematic, split into a 5 % strain block (a–a₃) and a 7 % strain block (b–b₃).
Panel (a) is an SEM image with a 20 μm scale bar in which two particles are boxed in red and reproduced as cropped insets labelled 'Particle 1 fracture' and 'Particle 2 fracture'.
Panels (a₁) and (b₁) carry a colourbar labelled 'Von-Mises equivalent strain' with printed limits 0.00 and 0.50 and ticks at 0.10 intervals.
Panels (a₂) and (b₂) carry a colourbar labelled 'PEEQ' with printed limits 0.000 and 0.500 and ticks at 0.000, 0.125, 0.250, 0.375, 0.500.

In panel (a₂) the highest plastic-equivalent strains (cyan-to-yellow) are concentrated immediately around the boxed particles, particularly the fractured ones, while the surrounding matrix stays dark blue (near zero).

Panel (a₃) plots σ₁₁ (MPa) on a 0–1000 axis against Engineering strain (%) on a 0–14 axis, with legend entries 'Particle 1' and 'Particle 2' and arrows labelled 'Fracture' at the abrupt stress drops of both curves.

Panel (b₃) plots σ₁₁ versus Engineering strain with a y-axis extending to 1800 MPa (top printed value 1800) and legend entries 'Particle 3' and 'Particle 4'; the grey Particle 3 curve falls only gradually and is arrow-labelled 'Decohesion', whereas the red Particle 4 curve drops sharply and is arrow-labelled 'Fracture'.

Panel (c)'s legend defines the symbols: TiB₂ Particle (yellow), δ-Ferrite (light-blue ellipse), Austenite (white pentagon), Plastic slip band (magenta line), Dislocation (⊥ symbol), TiB₂ Particle cracking void (yellow block with black crack) and Interfacial debonding void (yellow block with void).
Particle 1 fractured at 4.05 % global strain and Particle 2 fractured prematurely at 1.1 % global strain; each abrupt drop in σ₁₁ corresponds to that particle's fracture event.

The citing text states that good correspondence is observed between the experimental (μ-DIC) and simulated (FE) strain maps, both revealing a distinct strain gradient near particles, particularly surrounding fractured particles.

The citing text states that at 5 % global strain material damage arises primarily from particle breakage, and that the fractured particles likely contained significant initial defects giving them relatively low fracture strength.
The citing text states that particle fracture tends to accelerate final specimen failure more than particle decohesion does.

The caption asserts that the figure compares particle-behaviour percolation observed in FE simulations and experiments at 5 % and 7 % global engineering strain, with (a₃)/(b₃) giving σ₁₁ stress history for the particles marked in the SEM and μ-DIC panels.
No numeric stress or strain values are printed on the σ₁₁ curves themselves; the curves can only be read against the axis gridlines.
